newsitem.title: USA: Reports of Saudi plane deal premature -- White House.
newsitem.headline: Reports of Saudi plane deal premature -- White House.

text.p: The White House said Thursday it was premature to believe that a new deal for Saudi Arabia to buy U.S.-built planes worth up to $30 billion had been reached.

"There is a lot of enthusiasm in a lot of places for the idea, but we have received no official request or contract for that kind of sale from the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia," White House spokesman Mike McCurry told reporters.
The Washington Times reported Thursday that the Saudis wanted to buy as many as 100 Lockheed Martin Corp F-16 jet fighters, and that the deal could be worth up to $30 bln.
Prince Sultan, the Saudi defense and aviation minister, is expected to visit Washington next month.

A White House official who asked not to be identified said he could neither confirm or deny that such a deal was in the works. "The story has bubbled up before and nothing came of it. It may or may not be true this time," he said.
